_comment: Verdicts on flags raised by scripts/audit_check_scope.py. The audit is a heuristic and says so; without this file its next run reports the same flags and the work is done again. The audit refuses when an entry here names a check that no longer exists, so this file cannot rot into a list of names nobody can act on.

examined.why: This IS the denominator guard for the checks above it.
This IS the canary: it asserts something is still ignored, so the check beside it can distinguish a working ignore file from an empty one.
Asserts inequalities; a signature function returning a constant fails here.

One-sided alone, but paired with the inequality check below it and with test_signature_matches_ground_truth, which compares against data/sample/ground_truth.json. That file states in its own _comment that it is hand-computed, so the trio is not circular.
2026-09-02: read graphs[:200] of collections holding 306 to 5000 -- twelve per cent of the data behind a claim about all of it. Injection: a parallel edge at graph 300.
A unit test on a two-edge fixture; the module-level glob is what the heuristic saw.
Added 2026-09-02 to tie this scan to the artefact the paper quotes. It asserts the profile is non-empty before comparing three totals; the module-level glob is what the heuristic saw.
2026-09-02: asserted >=, which equality satisfies, on a collection where the term provably cannot act -- both sides scored 0.666667 there. Now strict, on a collection where it can.
2026-09-02: passed over an empty builder.
2026-09-02: globbed *.png only, so a leftover .pdf or .svg was invisible, and passed over an empty directory. Injection: a stray .svg, caught.

Replaces test_the_builder_declares_the_figures_the_draft_cites (renamed 2026-09-11, its verdict left behind naming a dead check). The old reason -- the cited set is a non-empty literal -- no longer applies: the set is now read from the generator's copy map, and the check asserts it is non-empty before taking the difference. Refutable: dropping one figure from the builder's FIGURES makes it fail, naming that figure; the unaltered builder passes. Not flagged by the audit, reviewed by hand because two or more asserts count as a guard there.

Replaces test_the_draft_refers_to_each_figure_it_should (renamed 2026-09-11, verdict 'as above' left behind). Fed six altered drafts, the rewritten check caught three: a figure commented out with % still counted as on the page, and an include written hinh/x.pdf was invisible, so a stale picture passed. It also read only ban_thao.tex after manuscript.tex became the submission version. Now strips comments, reports every include argument outside hinh/<name>, and runs on each draft present. 14 of 14 altered drafts behave as they should across both drafts, including an escaped \% that must not read as a comment.
2026-09-02: an empty baseline list reported every baseline as declared.
2026-09-02: 0 == 0 == 0 on an empty pool. Denominator asserted.
A differential test: two distinct code paths must agree at rho = 1.
Indexes graphs[1]; an empty result raises rather than passing.

2026-09-02: compared only the count, which any selection rule satisfies. Now checks which molecule came back. That turned up a real property, pinned in the test beside it: the weight scale depends on the subset loaded.
Literal expected values written by hand.
Asserts more than one distinct start across eight seeds; an empty result collapses to one element and fails.
Strict inequality between two different inputs; a constant function fails it.
Hand-computed expected set; an empty front fails it.
As above.
Runs against a real bare remote and asserts the push landed.
As above.
Builds a scratch repository, runs the real script, and matches its output contract. A tool that printed nothing would fail it.
As above.

The literals are the exit code, the script's output markers and a filename the test itself writes; the claim is read from a real bare remote. Refutable: against the publisher as it was before 2026-09-25 it fails (the commit stays local and [nothing] is printed).
As above: the remote is read, not assumed. Fails against the pre-2026-09-25 publisher, which never names the unpushed commit.
Asserts the refusal on both paths and reads the file back from the remote. Refutable: with the code-commit guard disabled it fails, and it is the only test that does.
Asserts a hand-derived ordering between the two sections; the defect it was written for violated exactly that ordering.
Asserts more than one distinct route across twelve seeds.
As above.
2026-09-02: scanned *.py under three named directories, 112 of 351 tracked files. Now identified by what git tracks, and it refuses rather than falling back to a narrower scan.
As above, and rescoped to what actually prints to a console: applying the encoding rule to Markdown would fail on one prose minus sign no console will ever see.
Asserts hand-counted cardinalities -- one for the star, three for the chain -- independent of the function under test.
Compares two different functions, and asserts an inequality first.

Computes the argmax from the objective's definition and compares it with a measurement read from the artefact; the literals it matches are the model's parameters, not the answer. Discriminating: sum mode yields three distinct predictions and matches 14 of 14. Refutable: raising gamma from 0.1 to 2.0 makes it wrong on 14 of 14.
Same shape as the check above: both sides come from artefacts, and the constants are the model's own parameters.
